essay.draft:
Nowadays there are many laws that we need to follow as a civilians. It is clear that most of them were created in order to build safe and healthy society. Nevertheless, this is double-age sword: this abundance of rules which individuals have to follow could foster a lot of questions towards governments. As for me, I do not think that it is neccessary to have this many. This essay argues the reasons why society needs to be regulated not only by law but by other ways too.

To begin with, restrictions that countries create will not work until they are explained. There are always ways to avoid something banned, and it is almost impossible to control it completely: which is proved by social network limitations in Russia. Instagram, Youtube and other servises still in use despite the fact that they are prohibited. In this case habits are stronger than imposed rules. Each action requires an proper explanation why it needs to be executed, otherwise citizens will be reluctant to do it whether it is a good deed or not. With that said a handful of rules will not help if it is not supported by motivation and understanding of the way humanity are likely to behave. 

Moreover, it will be helpful only if society trust their authorities. There are several examples of governments trying to earn as much money as possible by taxing. For instance, they could state rules and charge money not to build safety but in order to have higher margin. This is why I suppose that society needs to learn how to regulate independently. 

To conclude, I think that people protection is important but has to have its own limitations. Not always law is enough to avoid danger.
essay.revised:
Governments today impose a wide range of rules aimed at protecting citizens, from mandatory seatbelts to bans on smoking in public places. While such regulations are generally well-intentioned, I largely agree that there are too many of them, since a considerable number of these rules fail to achieve their purpose and, in some cases, exist for reasons other than genuine protection. This essay will argue that adding more rules rarely improves compliance without public trust, and that not all regulations are introduced purely for safety.

One reason there are too many unnecessary rules is that simply multiplying regulations rarely makes people comply with them. Rules only change behaviour when citizens understand and accept the reasoning behind them; when they do not, people tend to find ways around a rule regardless of how strictly it is enforced. In Russia, for example, platforms such as Instagram and YouTube remain officially banned, yet millions continue to access them daily via VPNs, showing that the existence of a rule does not by itself change what people actually do. If even a clearly enforced rule can be circumvented so easily, adding further rules on top of it achieves little beyond lengthening an already excessive list.

A second reason concerns the motives behind many regulations, since not all of them are created purely to protect the public. Governments sometimes introduce rules explicitly framed around safety or the environment but designed primarily to generate revenue through fines or taxes, which undermines both their legitimacy and public trust in regulation more broadly. A tax presented as an environmental measure, for instance, may do little to actually change behaviour if its real purpose is simply to raise government income, yet it still adds to the overall volume of rules citizens are expected to follow. When a meaningful share of existing rules serve purposes unrelated to genuine protection, it becomes difficult to justify their sheer number.

In conclusion, I largely agree that there are too many rules, not because protecting citizens is unimportant, but because a considerable number of existing regulations are either ineffective without public trust or introduced for reasons other than safety. Focusing on fewer, better-understood rules would likely serve society more effectively than continually adding new ones.

essay.draft:
The rise of online shopping has led to the closure of many local retail stores in cities and towns. What are the reasons for this trend, and what measures can be taken to support small businesses?

Nowadays people tend to make purchases online rather than offline and this trend is only becoming more spreadheaded every year. I suppose it was caused by several reasons, such as the pandemic in 2020 and new customer’s habits. In these conditions of changing market there are some actions that can help small businesses to keep themselves floating - for instance, lower taxes or new markeing tools. This essay will consider it closer. 

To begin with, we can see changes in patterns of decision making that are used by purchasers over last couple of years. It can be explained by Covid-19 and lockdown that made us sit at our homes for long months, and avoid interpersonal communication. It editted indivisual’s habits drastically. For example, we do not go for grocery shopping anymore - we just order delivery. Moreover, the market responded respectively and it caused the growth of marketplaces (e.g. Wildberries, Ozon, Yandex Market). It is not neccessary go to Zara in order to buy clothes because you are able to find anything through the Internet. That leads us to vanishing of small businesses into the thin air.

However, there are some measures that could be taken to support enterpreneurs. For example, the government can provide lower taxes. One of the causes of closing is high expences for businesmen and it would be helpful to make it less harmful. Another way is to find a method to adopt and be more flexible. Small businesses need fresh approaches to their marketing in case to gain new customers. Something that will overcome the advantage of easy and fast purchase in two clicks. They can use fidgital marketing or something that offer emotions instead of just boring buying process. For example, photobooth or lottery in their spots. 

To summarise, these are obvious trend towards the online retail that was caused by the pandemic and the development of technologies. At the same time it could come in handy for small businesses if they change the way they look at it.
